Notice that the numerator is proportional to the derivative of the denominator. So, we introduce the new variable $u={e}^{2x}-2x.$ Differentiating gives 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2{e}^{2x}-2=2({e}^{2x}-1)\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=({e}^{2x}-1)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{e}^{2x}-1}{{e}^{2x}-2x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{e}^{2x}-2x}\cdot ({e}^{2x}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡|{e}^{2x}-2x|}{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
